title: Transactional archive consumer and source-scoped Customers/Orders Data Vault pilot
decisions: Use PostgreSQL 18.6 in Docker with pinned images, persistent storage, SCRAM authentication and separate schema-owner, loader and reader roles.
Read completion manifests, including mixed-table batches; validate raw bytes before any business-data writes.
Commit the event journal, hubs, links, satellites, current pointers and batch ledger in one PostgreSQL transaction protected by a writer advisory lock.
Deduplicate by source-event identity as well as batch identity. Snapshot identity is generation-specific; stream identity is independent of capture clocks and batch boundaries.
Use source-scoped CustomerID and OrderID as pilot keys until application owners establish enterprise business-key semantics.

Retain one append-only satellite row for each distinct source CDC event, including deletes, and retain full descriptive attributes in JSONB with hashdiffs. This event-history policy is explicit; it is not a claim that every Data Vault must use the same physical design.
Derive current rows and relationships from source-position ordering, not object-listing order, load time or maximum receipt LSN.
Separate SQL-object inventory and migration from table capture. Definitions and dependencies are exported for review, not automatically translated.
Use a bounded Python COPY-based consumer for the measured pilot; assess Spark after representative volume and performance measurements. Keep the worker runnable once for later Airflow orchestration.
limits: Two-table pilot only; mixed-batch ignored-event counts explicitly record unconsumed tables.
Batch atomicity does not guarantee visibility of a whole source transaction spanning multiple archive batches.

Current views are partially visible during initial load; reconciliation must gate application cutover and downstream publication. Full-prefix discovery and an in-memory completed-key set require redesign/measurement at large batch counts.
Routine polling trusts completed ledger entries; full archive re-verification requires replay or a separate integrity audit.
Source instance, selected tables and snapshot/archive generation changes require an explicit versioned migration/backfill.
SQL Server dependency catalogs cannot establish all application consumers, dynamic SQL usage or ownership.
Single-VM resource caps and private network connections without intra-VM PostgreSQL TLS are lab simplifications; no production sizing, high availability or off-VM recovery is claimed.
No safe purge checkpoint or decommissioning authorization is produced.
